title: What games would you build if every NPC could remember, act on its own, stay in character and run offline, with no LLM in the loop? It's live, free for a week.
author: tyn_21
selftext:
I built an SDK where you give a character a personality, what they can do, and what they must never do. From there they notice events, remember what happened, form role-bounded goals, take plain-language commands from players, and carry consequences forward.

• No LLM in the brain. Reflexes, memory, and acting run in your build, offline, in milliseconds, at no cost per thought. Nothing on the frame ever waits on a network.  
• Planning is one small hosted call, and it runs no LLM either.  
• Dialogue is the one place a language model appears, and it's your LLM of choice, on your key or a free local model. The brain that moves the body and makes the plans never uses one.  
• The brain is under half a megabyte, trained with a research technique I developed.  
• Rules are enforced. A "never" is checked when the level loads, not hoped for at play.  
• Every decision writes a receipt. When an ally turns on you, you can replay which moments did it.  
• New behavior on request. Describe what you need and it comes back trained and tested. You never touch machine learning.

One CLI, one manifest, one websocket into your engine. An MCP server so your coding agent can drive it. Ships as one folder; players install nothing. Seven days free, no card, then $20 a month.

Site: https://canonopy.com  
Discord: https://discord.gg/VkgdCcxjrH  
What would this let you build?

comments.author: curious_biped_dev
comments.body:
The split between deterministic brain and LLM-for-dialogue-only is a smart way to keep cost and latency off the critical path. I went a simpler route on my own project, s[TOR-Y]telling: Closed Loop, where a local Llama-class model runs entirely on the player's PC and drives a whole cast (up to nine) reacting to the player and each other, no account, no per-message cost either, just less separation between reasoning and speech than what you built.

Curious how your planning call behaves under multiplayer-style scenes with several characters needing goals at once. Does it queue, or can they plan in parallel without stepping on each other's state?

replies.author: tyn_21
replies.body:
Closed Loop sounds clean, and fusing reasoning and speech is the right call if you're already paying for the local model's VRAM anyway. I split them because I wanted the decision path to survive a player trying to talk a character out of her rules, which is hard when one model does both.

On your question, they plan in parallel in one round trip. Characters needing a plan in the same sweep queue locally, and the batch flushes as a single request the moment any of them is about to act. Nine characters is one call, not nine.

They can't step on each other's state because the service holds none. Each wake runs against a throwaway journal containing exactly what that request shipped, with that character's own state row installed and handed back in the response. Any replica can answer any wake, and nothing about a character lives server-side between calls.

The tick never waits either. A healthy round trip lands in the same tick; a slow one goes to a background thread and lands a tick or two later, with that character's wake parked and retried on her next update.

One thing you might find interesting: it's one brain for the whole cast, not a model per character. Who someone is comes from their personality, their can/never list and their own memory, fed in at decision time.
